scenario: [NCBK.2.6]: TIMER_ARMED belongs to the rule-level cooldown alone, and the engine emits none for the gate of a `cooldown:` on a `call` ([LCRS.8.2]), whether it admits the call or not. `r`'s only cooldown is on its call. At 0 s Trig k=1 n=0 is asserted and pumped: the gate admits, so the stream has the call and RULE_FIRE_END with no TIMER_ARMED after it. At 2 s n becomes 1, a mutable-slot change under the same key, so the same activation key: the rule fires and brackets, the gate suppresses the call, and again no TIMER_ARMED. `twin cooldown 10_s` is the rule-level twin these differ from, as in NCBK.2.6_timer_armed_only_when_admitted: its admitted firing has TIMER_ARMED after its RULE_FIRE_END. It is also what lets this vector read the absence: an event_sequence judges only the kinds it names ([RCTS.1.2.10]), so timer_armed is named by the one event that has it, and any other TIMER_ARMED on the stream fails the vector. Kinds stated: rule_fire_begin, action_call, action_log, rule_fire_end, timer_armed. PATH PINNED: each runtime's emit site, reached through the stream callback. In libds, `_rete_after_fire` (engine_rete_adapters.c) emits only on `rm->has_cool`, the rule-level window. In the Mercury runtime, `ncbk_2_6_timer_armed` (ds.exec.m) reads the rule's `rc_cooldown` alone.
rules_ds:
service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    no response

schema Trig scope logical:
    k: Int key
    n: Int mutable

schema Twin scope logical:
    k: Int key

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    call svc.read n: t.n cooldown: 10_s

rule twin cooldown 10_s:
    Twin w
->
    log info "twin {w.k}"
